post.description: Create a new event log draft.

get.description:
List event logs.

- ``?published=true``  — only currently-live versions.
- ``?published=false`` — only names with no live version yet.
- no param            — latest row per name (default).

schema.title: Response Get All Event Logs Api V1 Registry Event Logs  Get

get.description: Latest row for the name (draft if one exists, else published, else most recent historic).

put.description:
Apply an edit.

If a draft already exists, mutates it in place. Otherwise spawns a new
draft on top of the currently-published (or most recent historic) row.
The currently-published row is **untouched** — what's live in Redis stays
live until the customer hits publish.

delete.description:
Delete the event log and all its history.

Rejected with 400 if a row is currently published — the customer must
unpublish first. Otherwise drafts and historic rows are removed wholesale.

Discard the pending draft for an event log.

Deletes only the draft row; the currently-published version (if any) is
untouched. Returns 404 if the event log does not exist or has no draft.

get.description:
Check whether batch sync is complete for a published attribute group.

Returns ``"completed"`` status when every expected sync interval for every
attribute has been completed by the batch engine, ``"running"`` otherwise.

Returns 404 if the attribute group does not exist.
Returns 400 if the attribute group exists but is not published.

post.summary: Tests attribute groups by running a query on the atomic events table in the warehouse on a small window and returns the results as a dataframe.

schema.title: Response Test View Api V1 Testing Attribute Groups  Post

post.summary: Tests interventions by running a query on the warehouse with criteria filtering applied in SQL.
post.description:
Execute the attribute group query for the view(s) referenced in the intervention's
criteria, wrap in a CTE, apply the criteria as a WHERE clause in the warehouse,
and return the filtered results. Supports one or more attribute groups (views);
when multiple are referenced, they must all use the same attribute key.

status.title: Status
status.description: 'completed' when every expected sync interval for every attribute in the group has status 'completed' in sync_log. 'failed' when any expected interval has status 'failed'. 'running' when any interval is still pending or running (and none have failed), or when the batch engine has not been deployed yet.

streaming_since.title: Streaming Since
streaming_since.description: UTC timestamp when streaming started for this group — the latest streaming_since_tstamp across all attributes. None if no attribute has been published for streaming.

last_synced_at.title: Last Synced At
last_synced_at.description: UTC timestamp of the most recent completed sync — the latest updated_at across completed intervals. None if nothing has completed yet.

sync_started_at.title: Sync Started At
sync_started_at.description: UTC start of the earliest in-flight (running) interval, surfaced while syncing to gauge progress. None when no interval is currently running.

data_fresh_through.title: Data Fresh Through
data_fresh_through.description: UTC timestamp the warehouse data is fresh through — the latest interval_end across completed intervals. Applies to warehouse and external-batch groups only; always None for stream groups.

source_table.title: Source Table
source_table.description: Fully-qualified warehouse table the sync reads from (db.schema.table). None if no sync has recorded a source table yet.

sync_progress.description: Progress through the expected sync window, in days. Applies to all batch-syncing groups, including external batch. None when the group has no expected sync window (e.g. no attributes or fields).

errors.title: Errors
errors.description: Failed sync intervals within the group's expected windows, each with its interval start/end and error message, deduplicated per interval across the group's attributes. Most recent first (by interval start). Always present; empty unless status is 'failed'.

SyncError.title: SyncError
SyncError.description:
A single failed sync interval and the error it failed with.

One entry per failed interval, scoped to the attribute group's expected
sync windows and deduplicated across the group's member attributes (a
warehouse failure that hits several attributes in the same interval is
reported once). The interval bounds locate the failure in time; the client
renders them directly rather than as a day index.

days_synced.title: Days Synced
days_synced.description: Number of days of the expected sync window that have completed.

days_failed.title: Days Failed
days_failed.description: Number of days within the window that have a failed interval.

days_total.title: Days Total
days_total.description: Total length of the expected sync window, in days.

SyncProgress.title: SyncProgress
SyncProgress.description:
How much of the expected sync window has completed, in calendar days.

Expressed in days, not sync intervals. Today one interval is one day, but
that is an implementation detail of the batch engine and may change; the
contract is always stated in days.

A day's status is the worst case across every attribute in the group that
spans it (failed > pending > synced): the day counts as ``failed`` if any
attribute failed it, otherwise ``synced`` only if every attribute completed
it, otherwise it is still pending. The three counts reconcile exactly, so
``days_synced + days_failed + days_pending == days_total`` (``days_pending``
is derived by subtraction and not surfaced), and ``days_synced ==
days_total`` precisely when the group status is ``completed`` — independent
of differing per-attribute window lengths.

signals_api__models__intervention__crite.title: Criterion
signals_api__models__intervention__crite.description:
A single logic clause used to evaluate if a rule-based intervention should be triggered.

Evaluated as an expression of the form: <attribute value> <operator> <value>

Value can generally be any JSON-serializable scalar primitive.
Value is optional for the "is null" and "is not null" operators.
If value is scalar for the "in" and "not in" operators, the operand order is reversed, with the attribute value considered an array and checked for containing the scalar.
"like" and "not like" use SQL-like pattern matches, with % and _ as multi/single character wildcards, respectively. There is no escape method.
References to unpopulated attributes will evaluate to false unless the operator is "is null".
